'''Andrea Lübcke''' (born 9 December 1978) is a German politician for [[Alliance 90/The Greens]]. She has been the state chairwoman of {{Interlanguage link|Alliance 90/The Greens Brandenburg|de|Bündnis 90/Die Grünen Brandenburg}} since March 2025 and a [[member of the German Bundestag]] since July 2025.

== Life ==
Lübcke grew up in the small [[Mecklenburg]] town of [[Brüel]]. She lives with her family in [[Eichwalde]] and has two sons.<ref name="ueber">{{cite web |access-date=2025-04-03 |author=Andrea Lübcke |title=Über mich |url=https://andrea-luebcke.de/ueber-mich/ |archive-date=8 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251008140409/https://andrea-luebcke.de/ueber-mich/ |url-status=live }}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

=== Scientific career ===
After [[Abitur|graduating from high school]] in Brüel in 1997, Andrea Lübcke studied [[physics]] at the [[Friedrich Schiller University of Jena]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Dr. Andrea Lübcke |url=https://www.gruene-bundestag.de/abgeordnete/details/dr-andrea-luebcke/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=www.gruene-bundestag.de |language=de |archive-date=10 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250910174033/https://www.gruene-bundestag.de/abgeordnete/details/dr-andrea-luebcke/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After a six-month research internship at the [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] in [[California]], USA, she graduated in 2002 with a diploma thesis on "Utilizing the [[Gerhard Borrmann|Borrmann]] effect to develop an ultrafast switch in the X-ray range." From 2002 onward, she worked as a doctoral student at the Institute of Optics and Quantum Electronics at the Friedrich Schiller University of Jena. In 2007, she received her [[Dr. rer. nat.|doctorate]] with a [[thesis]] on time-resolved [[X-ray diffraction]] on [[High-temperature superconductivity|high-temperature superconductors]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}}

From 2007 to 2019, Lübcke worked as a [[scientist]] at various research institutions in [[Germany]] and [[Switzerland]], including the [[Free University of Berlin]], the {{Interlanguage link|Max Born Institute|de|Max-Born-Institut für Nichtlineare Optik und Kurzzeitspektroskopie}}, the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne]], and the [[Paul Scherrer Institute]]. From 2019 to 2021, she was a lecturer in [[optics]] and [[photonics]] at the Institute of Optics and Atomic Physics at the [[Technical University of Berlin]].<ref name=":0" />

In 2021, she moved to scientific policy consulting at the German Academy of Science and Engineering ([[Acatech]]). Until 2025, she was responsible for leading projects on the development of the [[hydrogen economy]] and innovation ecosystems for fusion technologies.<ref name=":0" />

=== Political career ===
Lübcke became a member of Alliance 90/The Greens in 2018.<ref name="ueber" /> Since 2019, she has been a member of the [[Eichwalde]] [[Municipal council (Germany)|municipal council]] and the [[Dahme-Spreewald]] [[District council (Germany)|district council]]. She has been chairwoman of the Green Party [[Fraktion (Bundestag)|faction]] in the municipal council since 2019, and in the district council since 2023.{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}}

From 2020 to 2023, she was an advisory board member of the Dahme-Spreewald district association of Alliance 90/The Greens. On 15 March 2025, Lübcke was elected co-state chairwoman of the Greens in Brandenburg.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Redaktion |title=Landtagswahl: Grüne nominieren Eichwalderin Lübcke {{!}} Der Schulzendorfer |url=https://www.schulzendorfer.de/landtagswahl-gruene-nominieren-eichwalderin-luebcke/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |language=de-DE}}</ref>

In the [[2024 Brandenburg state election]], Lübcke ran as a direct candidate for Alliance 90/The Greens in the [[Dahme-Spreewald I]] constituency and was ranked 19th on the [[State list (Germany)|state list]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-13 |title=Wirtschaft trifft Politik |url=https://gruene-dahme-spreewald.de/blog/2024/06/13/pressemitteilung-2/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=gruene-dahme-spreewald.de |language=de |archive-date=15 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251015172811/https://gruene-dahme-spreewald.de/blog/2024/06/13/pressemitteilung-2/ |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the Greens were unable to win a [[direct mandate]] statewide and failed to clear the [[five percent hurdle]] to re-enter the [[Landtag of Brandenburg]].

In the [[2025 German federal election]], Lübcke ran as a [[direct candidate]] in the constituency of [[Dahme-Spreewald – Teltow-Fläming III]] and in third place on the [[State list (Germany)|state list]] of the Greens in Brandenburg. In her [[Bundestag constituencies|constituency]], she came fifth with 5.2 percent of the [[first vote]]s after the candidates of the [[AfD]], [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|CDU]], [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|SPD]] and [[Die Linke|The Left]], and was thus unsuccessful.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bundestagswahl 2025: Diese Kandidaten treten im Wahlkreis 62 in Dahme-Spreewald an |url=https://www.moz.de/nachrichten/brandenburg/bundestagswahl-2025-diese-kandidaten-treten-im-wahlkreis-62-in-dahme-spreewald-an-77769177.html |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=www.moz.de |language=de}}</ref> Since only the first two places from her party's state list were successful, she initially failed to enter the [[German Bundestag]]. After [[Annalena Baerbock]] resigned from her mandate to take up the role of [[President of the United Nations General Assembly]], Lübcke took her place in the German Bundestag on 1 July 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gellner |first=Torsten |date=2025-03-19 |title=UN-Job für Baerbock: Nachrückerin Andrea Lübcke ist Physikerin aus Eichwalde |url=https://www.maz-online.de/brandenburg/un-job-fuer-baerbock-nachrueckerin-andrea-luebcke-ist-physikerin-aus-eichwalde-CDL4RCSPSVDTHHJUJGFKIU65NQ.html |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=www.maz-online.de |language=de |archive-date=23 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723231929/https://www.maz-online.de/brandenburg/un-job-fuer-baerbock-nachrueckerin-andrea-luebcke-ist-physikerin-aus-eichwalde-CDL4RCSPSVDTHHJUJGFKIU65NQ.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In the Bundestag, Lübcke is the chairwoman of her parliamentary group in the {{Interlanguage link|Committee on Research, Technology, Space and Technology Assessment|de|Ausschuss für Forschung, Technologie, Raumfahrt und Technikfolgenabschätzung}}.

Upon her election to the Bundestag, Lübcke announced that she would resign from her position as state chairwoman in autumn 2025.{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}}
